requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1 (firewalld active, enabled, and permanent config in place)
requirements.summary: firewalld was already active/enabled at baseline; executor added persistent (--permanent) rules for ssh and 8080/tcp, set zone target to REJECT, and reloaded. /etc/firewalld/zones/public.xml on disk shows the persisted config, and post-reboot the same config was confirmed intact with firewalld active/enabled.

firewall-cmd --list-all shows ssh service allowed both at runtime and permanent; nftables filter_IN_public_allow chain accepts tcp dport 22; sshd confirmed listening and healthy pre- and post-restart.

firewall-cmd shows 8080/tcp added and persisted; nftables allow chain accepts tcp dport 8080; live curl test to the node's external IP on 8080 returned HTTP 200 confirming functional reachability through the zone rules.

Zone target set to %%REJECT%%; nftables filter_IN_public chain falls through to 'reject with icmpx admin-prohibited' for traffic not matching the allow chain (only 22/8080). Pre-existing unrelated allowances (cockpit, dhcpv6-client) were removed so only ssh+8080 remain. The self-curl test on port 9999 returned content rather than a clean rejection, but this is explained and consistent with loopback (iifname lo accept) bypassing the public-zone chain rather than a real misconfiguration — the nftables ruleset directly shows the reject fallback applies to the eth0-bound public zone.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (4a743885...) and firewalld health captured; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; subsequent poll timed out confirming disconnect; post-restart boot_id (2a24f144...) differs, confirmed by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots as well; firewalld, persisted zone config, nftables rules, and sshd were all re-verified healthy after the restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — a persistent firewalld configuration on node1 permitting only SSH and 8080/tcp while rejecting other inbound traffic — are directly supported by firewall-cmd, nftables, and live-port evidence, and the configuration was confirmed to survive an actual node restart (differing boot_id, recovered firewalld/nftables/sshd state). The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with clear pre/post boot-identity and health evidence. The only blemish is a handful of leftover temporary test-listener log/pid files in /tmp, a low-severity, non-security-impacting residue.
limitations: The self-curl test intended to prove an unrelated port (9999) is blocked was inconclusive because same-host curl traverses the loopback interface, which bypasses the public-zone chain; unrelated-port rejection instead relies on nftables ruleset inspection rather than a live external-connection test.
No evidence was captured from a genuinely external client verifying SSH/8080 reachability or unrelated-port rejection from outside the node itself; all functional tests were run locally on node1.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were limited to the firewalld reconfiguration (required), removal of unrelated pre-existing service allowances (required to satisfy the 'reject unrelated' outcome), temporary test HTTP listeners on 8080/9999 used for bounded functional verification, and the restart itself. The test listeners were killed and confirmed absent from the socket table (cmd-f766d31253d84359, cmd-a6b52ea9171c46ac), but their log/pid files (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid, /tmp/http9999.log, /tmp/http9999.pid) remained in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot as minor uncleaned residue — low-risk and non-functional but not fully reverted.
